title: Aviation Daily Brief
headline: An emergency directive on HX-35 fan blades lands on an engine supply chain that is already the narrowbody market's tightest constraint.
summary: Regulator mandates ultrasonic fan blade inspections on about 380 HX-35 engines within 50 cycles; expect added pressure on shop capacity already running at ~125-day turnarounds.
Northwind Air firms 24 Meridian M-220s (+12 options) to upgauge regional-jet routes from 2028; the same engine type is on the order.
Meridian lifts M-220 output to 9/month and keeps a 12/month target for end-2027, naming titanium forgings as the binding risk.
Q3 traffic shows transatlantic fares falling for the first time since 2024 while domestic unit revenue keeps rising on constrained capacity.

sections.title: Safety & regulation
sections.takeaway: One emergency directive with direct fleet and MRO consequences.

items.headline: Emergency AD: repeat ultrasonic inspections on HX-35 fan blades
items.so_what: ~380 engines must be inspected within 50 cycles and every 400 thereafter; six hours per on-wing check adds overnight maintenance load for M-220 operators.
items.detail: Root cause traced so far to a shot-peening deviation at a sub-tier supplier; blade replacement expected as terminating action.

sources.title: Airworthiness directive mandates repeat fan blade inspections on HX-35 engines

sections.title: Airlines
sections.takeaway: Upgauging and long-thin international routes on narrowbodies.

items.headline: Northwind Air firms 24 Meridian M-220s, options for 12 more
items.so_what: Replaces 31 regional jets on dense domestic routes from Q2 2028; capex guidance unchanged.
items.detail: HX-35 engines selected with a ten-year maintenance agreement - now exposed to the new fan blade directive.

sources.title: Northwind Air firms up order for 24 Meridian M-220 aircraft

items.headline: Transatlantic yields soften as capacity returns
items.so_what: Load factors held near 87% but fares fell year on year; expect off-peak transatlantic trims and redeployment to leisure markets.

sections.title: Manufacturers & supply chain
sections.takeaway: Rates are rising, but forgings and engine hot sections still set the pace.

items.so_what: Second final assembly line open; 12/month target for end-2027 reaffirmed with titanium forgings as the main risk.

items.headline: Engine shop turnaround passes 120 days
items.so_what: HPT blades and vanes are the most common hold; spare engine lease rates up ~40% in a year.
